units.notes: This pass looked only at the plant's location. The unit's other fields were handled in the first look and are not repeated here.

Latitude.note:
This sets the point for Union Depot Energy Center. The new point is 44.23250, -88.11630. It is the combined cycle power block inside the site fence that the developer drew in its application to the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin.

Where the site is:
- The joint application for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity, filed November 6, 2026 in docket 5-CE-162, is at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=617707. On page 20 of the file, section 7.11.1, it says 'The Proposed Site is located in Section 04, Township 20 North, Range 20 East. The permanent footprint of the Proposed Site is approximately 85 acres.'
- Section 7.11.2 on the same page says construction traffic will enter the site from County Road K.

Where the plant sits inside the site:
- Appendix L of the application is a zip file of mapping data, at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=617796. Its layer 'Proposed_Site_Footprint' is one shape of 84.8 acres. It runs from 44.22705 to 44.23355 north and from -88.12044 to -88.11390 east. Its layer 'Proposed_Site_Fence_Line' is the fenced area, from 44.22763 to 44.23347 north and from -88.11894 to -88.11426 east.
- The site layout drawing in Appendix A, 'Proposed Site GA', is at https://apps.psc.wi.gov/ERF/ERFview/viewdoc.aspx?docid=617756. Page 2 of the file is drawing GA001, revision J, titled 'Forest Junction Energy Center Union Depot Energy Center General Arrangement'. It is drawn on an air photo. The five simple cycle turbines of Forest Junction fill the middle and south of the fence. The one combined cycle unit of Union Depot is at the north end, with its gas turbine, heat recovery steam generator, stack, steam turbine and air cooled condenser fans.
- I laid the mapping layers over a satellite picture. The footprint matches the farm field north of County Road K, and the stormwater pond and the drainage swale line up with the drawing. Read against the pond and the fence, the center of the combined cycle block falls at about 44.23250, -88.11630. The imagery date is unknown, and the field is still bare farmland.
- The point is shown on a map at https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=44.23250,-88.11630.

Why the accuracy is exact:
- The point rests on the site footprint coordinates filed with the application, and the plant's own block is placed from the developer's site drawing. That is the manual's route for coordinates in a permit application or a similar document.

How far it moves:
- The point moves about 6.6 km from GEM's point 44.19000, -88.05800, which is near Brillion. It is about 500 m from the middle of the wetland survey area that the first look used.

location.location_route: The point comes from the site footprint coordinates in the mapping data filed with the developer's application to the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin, placed on the combined cycle block using the site layout drawing in the same filing.
location.review_note: The move is over 2 km, but it rests on the applicant's own filed site footprint and site drawing, which both agree with the satellite picture, so no further check is needed.

source_log.note: The application names the site as Section 04, Township 20 North, Range 20 East, with a footprint of about 85 acres, on page 20 of the file.
Appendix L mapping data. The file loads as a zip. I read the site footprint and fence line layers from it and converted them from the Wisconsin Transverse Mercator grid to latitude and longitude.
The site layout drawing GA001 revision J. It shows the combined cycle block at the north end of the fenced site.
The table that describes each mapping layer. It was used only to find the footprint layer.
Map link for the new point.
